summary: The v5 evaluation matches 34/45 screens, then stops at segment 0 step 34 when the Ranger selects a wished cursed scroll of teleportation with `r`, `g`. C accepts the scroll, reports that it disappears, and reaches the controlled level-teleport prompt on the next screen. `read.c:doread()` has no cursed-scroll rejection for a sighted hero; it calls `seffects()`, whose teleportation arm calls `level_tele()` for a cursed scroll. JS `read.js:doread()` rejects this valid case because `calmTeleport` requires an uncursed scroll and `confusedTeleport` only admits a blessed, noncursed scroll while confused. JS already has the cursed `seffect_teleportation()` → `level_tele()` arm, so the first missing branch is the `doread()` admission path. The remaining post-teleport movement and return-to-level inputs have not been replayed past this stop and are not claimed as matching evidence.

source.branch: A debug-mode Ranger wishes for a cursed teleportation scroll, then reads it while sighted and not confused. read.c:doread() passes the readable scroll through its generic scroll path; read.c:seffects() dispatches SCR_TELEPORTATION to seffect_teleportation(), which calls level_tele() because the scroll is cursed. The recipe then supplies level 2 at the controlled prompt. The saved C recording shows “As you read the scroll, it disappears.” at step 34, the level prompt at step 35, and “You materialize on a different level!” at step 37.
callers: cmd.c:1817 binds the `r` command to doread(). js/cmd.js:runReadCommand() calls js/read.js:doread(), and the `doread` dispatcher routes that result back through the command loop.
read.c:doread() obtains an object through getobj("read", read_ok, GETOBJ_PROMPT); C read_ok() suggests scrolls and spellbooks. The read-object selection prompt at case step 33 already matches.

read.c:doread() calls seffects(scroll) for ordinary scrolls and consumes its integer return to decide discovery and scroll cleanup. js/read.js currently calls its partial seffects() for the same source site.

read.c:seffects() dispatches SCR_TELEPORTATION to seffect_teleportation(&sobj); that helper chooses level_tele() for cursed or confused scrolls. The JS seffects() and seffect_teleportation() contain this source branch.
dependencies: For a whole doread() port, hack.c:check_capacity() returns the early ECMD_OK decision, invent.c:getobj() returns the selected scroll or cancellation, spell.c:study_book() returns whether reading spent a turn, and read.c:seffects() returns whether the scroll was consumed; those are all consumed return values. check_capacity(), getobj(), and study_book() already have JS implementations, but seffects() is explicitly partial and currently covers only a subset of read.c switch arms. The source-compliant whole-function scope must complete that return-valued seffects() dependency, not treat note_unported() as its result.

The selected seffects() arm calls read.c:seffect_teleportation(), a void helper. C read.c:2015-2032 and JS read.js:534-545 both route a cursed scroll to level_tele() and set gk.known; JS seffects() returns 0 so doread() retains responsibility for discovery and useup().

The selected level_tele() path is controlled because wizard mode is active: it consumes getlin() input "2", then consumes the boolean from apply.c:next_to_u() on the common tail before scheduling a goto. JS teleport.js has the corresponding call, and apply_next_to_u.js returns true for the case with no leashed companions or steed; its pet and mount branches remain explicit refusals, but are not reached by this recipe. The evaluation stops before JS executes level_tele(), so replay evidence is still needed.
The case continues with movement and an up-stairs command after arriving on level 2. Those later do.c movement/stair callers have not been diagnosed because the JS replay stops at the read branch.

evidence: The current saved queue .cache/v5-baseline-mismatch-queue.json identifies this case at evaluation d273b8936ba6746f4fa8287bf41668a9776c927c as 34/45 screens and cursors, 2744/5703 RNG calls, 11 unmatched screens; the first stop is step 34 with the selected-readable-object refusal.

The independent recipe challenges/cases/v5/ranger-level-teleport-return.recipe.session.json uses seed 90525073 and debug Ranger options. Its recorded inputs wish `cursed scroll of teleportation`, then read it with `r`, `g`, answer `2` to level_tele(), and continue with `jjjjl< `.

The C recording challenges/cases/v5/ranger-level-teleport-return.session.json has key `g` at segment 0 step 34 and screen text “As you read the scroll, it disappears.”; step 35 asks “To what level do you want to teleport?”; step 37 reports “You materialize on a different level!” and status level 2.

nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c:330-646 admits the selected sighted scroll, sets pickup_prev, and reaches seffects(scroll) without requiring !cursed. read.c:2015-2032 routes the cursed scroll to level_tele(); read.c:2194-2290 returns whether seffects consumed the scroll.

js/read.js:346-458 has the failing admission gate: ordinaryScroll requires !scroll.cursed, calmTeleport depends on ordinaryScroll, and confusedTeleport is limited to blessed, noncursed confused teleportation scrolls. The resulting UnsupportedReadError is emitted before scroll.pickup_prev changes.
cmd.c:1817 and js/cmd.js:3382, 5110-5111 wire the `r` entry to doread(). Existing JS seffect_teleportation() handles cursed scrolls at read.js:534-545, but the selected record does not reach it.

active: Read a cursed teleportation scroll while sighted and not confused: synthetic/v5/ranger-level-teleport-return, segment 0 step 34; C then takes read.c:doread() → seffects() → seffect_teleportation() → teleport.c:level_tele().
blocked: The JS doread() gate refuses every cursed teleportation scroll before C’s generic scroll path, so no JS replay evidence currently covers the cursed read or controlled level-teleport caller.
The recorded inputs after arrival on level 2 (jjjjl<) have not been source-attributed in a matching JS replay; diagnose their first difference after the read path is enabled.

The selected teleporter branch in level_tele() consumes the controlled destination input and the boolean result from apply.c:next_to_u() before scheduling the level change.
plannedWholeFunctionScope.scopeNote: This is missing behavior inside a partial source port, so selection policy calls for a file-port of the whole read.c:doread() function, not a divergence fix scoped only to its cursed-scroll admission gate.
